terms.comment: The word of the libellī; also a prop (Cato, Agr. 14).

phrases.latin: fulmentās calceōrum ad canthum rotae posteriōris admovet et terendō cursum tardat
phrases.english: he puts the heels of his shoes to the back tyre and slows down by rubbing

sources: Lewis & Short: fulmenta · Lewis & Short: fulmentum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 327.
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
